title: Language, Sexuality, Narrative: The Oresteia
author: Goldhill, Simon
subject: classics; Greek tragedy; Aeschylus; Oresteia; Aeschylus criticism; ancient Greek drama; literary theory; narratology; gender and sexuality in antiquity; Cambridge University Press; Simon Goldhill
description: First paperback edition (2004) of Goldhill's 1984 study, a close reading of Aeschylus' Oresteia that draws on modern literary theory and anthropology. Trade paperback in the pink Cambridge wrappers; no dust jacket, as issued. A very good copy, with three defects: a previous owner's name at the head of the title page has been struck out with a solid band of dark purple marker; the upper corner of the rear wrapper is creased and bumped, with light white scuffing to the laminate beside it; and a leaf in the bibliography at the rear carries a lengthwise crease. Otherwise the wrappers are bright and unfaded, the text is clean and unmarked, and the binding is tight and square.
